0.original: For all his comforting words, Alphinaud is plainly troubled by Master Chai's sudden disappearance.

48.original: Y'know, Eulmore's nothing like I thought it'd be. But somehow, I can't picture going anywhere else.

49.original: The Chais are part of it, I s'pose. They've been good to me. I only wish there was something more I could do to help them...

50.original: It makes no sense for Master Chai to have left without a word. But even if he had, he would not have done so unobserved.

51.original: <hex:021A020203>Someone<hex:021A020103> here will have seen something. I am sure of it.

52.original: We should split up and inquire as to whether anyone saw him leave or, failing that, if they have any idea where he might have gone. I will meet you at the Glory Gate to compare notes later on.

53.original: It would seem Master Chai paid a visit to the Beehive before taking his leave of Eulmore. Unfortunately, the patrons I spoke with were too deep in their cups to remember aught else.

54.original: ...You ever get the feeling you're being watched? Ahh, I'm probably just imagining things.

55.original: You find a shoebill gazing in Kai-Shirr's general direction. Silent. Vigilant. Plotting...?

56.original: Master Chai? Why yes, I spoke with him recently, though I recall he was in a rather dour mood. Concerned about Eulmore's neglect of industry, you see.

57.original: With Lord Vauthry's apparently inexhaustible stores of meol, and no great need for money, it's little wonder our businesses were all but forgotten under his rule.

58.original: But I assured Master Chai that the Boutique of Splendors will do all it can to contribute to the revival of trade here in Eulmore─which seemed to satisfy him. He took his leave soon after.

59.original: Your exchange with Mowen has taught you about “The stagnant state of business in Eulmore.”

60.original: Looking for Master Chai, are you? Is something amiss? When last I saw him, he seemed ready to collapse from exhaustion. I insisted he rest and catch his breath, and we talked for a while─about his concerns over the city's defenses amongst other things.

61.original: He made more than a few valid points. Many of our men are still recovering after your confrontation with Lord Vauthry, and finding General Ran'jit in a heap in the middle of the plaza shook us all to the core.

62.original: The man commanded no small amount of loyalty, and some of our longest-serving soldiers seemed lost without him. Indeed, a number of them left.

63.original: N-Not that we blame <hex:021A020203>you<hex:021A020103>, of course. Without you and yours, we would still be blind to the error of our ways.

64.original: Anyway...funding permitting, I proposed replenishing our ranks with volunteers from the Derelicts and Gatetown.

65.original: We have a duty to protect not only Eulmore, you see, but the surrounding regions of Kholusia as well, and I for one would welcome any man or woman willing to take up arms for that cause. Indeed, I told him as much, and he seemed relieved to hear it. It was on that note that we parted ways. He headed outside, as I recall.

66.original: Your exchange with Cornenne has taught you about “The perilous state of Eulmore's defenses.”

67.original: Aye, I recall a man fittin' that description. Asked to speak with the poor buggers lately come from Wright.

68.original: Said he wanted to know the state of things down in the Derelicts. And you can be sure we gave him an earful. Lack of food, medicine, clothin'─there was plenty to tell.

69.original: We hunt high and low for whatever we can scavenge, and it's barely enough to fill our bellies. But folk here don't just want to survive, they want to thrive!

70.original: When he heard that, he started mumblin' to himself. Somethin' about findin' us work, I think.

71.original: Fair play to him, though─not content with havin' his ear chewed about the Derelicts, he asked about the other settlements an' all. After that, I can't really say. Looked like he was headed for Gatetown when I last saw him.

72.original: Your exchange with Hathenbet has taught you about “The poor living conditions of Kholusia's downtrodden.”

73.original: I know not what Master Chai is planning, but if he intends to bring business back to Eulmore, he has my wholehearted support.

74.original: Master Chai seemed genuinely concerned over our lack of numbers. Would that we had the money to hire more guards...

75.original: What? I told you everythin' I know. If you're after that Chai bloke, you won't find him here.

76.original: Any luck? I got nowhere myself, but it sounds like Alphinaud might have.

77.original: Ah, there you are. How did you fare? Have you learned anything which might offer a clue as to Master Chai's whereabouts?

79.original: He apparently paid a visit to the Queen Bee as well.

80.original: They discussed the possibility of granting admission to customers from outside Eulmore, an idea to which the proprietor was surprisingly receptive.

81.original: Sounds like he's got big plans for the place. Eulmore, I mean─not the Bee.

82.original: Perhaps. But the question remains─where did he go after leaving the city?
